title: Representability and smoothness of the Picard space of a relative curve
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:C\to S$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with fibres of dimension at most one. Suppose the canonical map $\mathcal O_T\to(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{C_T}$ is an isomorphism for every $S$-scheme $T$, where $C_T=C\times_ST$ [def-pc-base-change]. The relative Picard fppf sheaf $P=\operatorname{Pic}_{C/S}$ [sk-def-picard-pic] is represented by a commutative group algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space] over $S$. The map $P\to S$ is smooth, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation, and its diagonal is an immersion. The group law is induced by tensor product of invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module]. For algebraic spaces, smoothness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts; quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact, and the immersion assertion is about the representable diagonal.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-picard-stack-curve-geometry] to $f:C\to S$. Its properness, flatness and finite presentation are precisely the stated hypotheses, and the fibre dimension bound supplies smoothness. Thus the category $\mathcal B_f$ of line bundles (retaining all automorphisms) is an algebraic stack smooth over $S$. This does not yet assert representability of its isomorphism-class sheaf.

For $L$ on $C_T$, a local trivialization identifies an endomorphism with multiplication by a local function. These functions agree on overlaps, so $\operatorname{Aut}(L)=\Gamma(C_T,\mathcal O_{C_T})^\times$. The assumed canonical isomorphism of structure sheaves identifies this naturally with $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)^\times$. Consequently $I_{\mathcal B_f/S}\to\mathcal B_f$ pulls back at every object over $T$ to $\mathbf G_{m,T}\to T$. On $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ this is $\operatorname{Spec}(A[z,w]/(zw-1))\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, of finite presentation. For a square-zero surjection $R'\to R$, lift a unit and its inverse to $a,b\in R'$. Write $ab=1+i$ with $i^2=0$; then $a$ is invertible with inverse $b(1-i)$. This lifts every map from an affine first-order thickening, proving formal smoothness and hence smoothness by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Smoothness implies flatness and local finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. All these identifications commute with base change, so the inertia projection has the hypotheses of the flat-inertia quotient theorem.

source.place: lemma-pic-inertia; examples-stacks.tex example-inertia-stack-of-picard; explicit square-zero unit lift

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-flat-inertia-algebraic-space-quotient], the sheaf $Q=(T\mapsto\operatorname{Pic}(C_T))^{\mathrm{fppf}}$ is an algebraic space smooth over $S$. Use the big site within a containing universe as in [def-pc-fppf-site]. The sheafification unit is locally bijective by [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection]: its associated-sheaf map is an isomorphism by the adjunction identities of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Thus sheaf sections locally have presheaf representatives and equality of their images is local equality. Identify $Q$ with $P$ of [sk-def-picard-pic]: every bundle pulled back from $T$ is trivial after a Zariski covering of $T$. Thus the maps from the presheaves $\operatorname{Pic}(C_T)$ and $\operatorname{Pic}(C_T)/f_T^*\operatorname{Pic}(T)$ have the same sheafification: locally lift a quotient class, and trivialize any base bundle witnessing a difference. This proves local surjectivity and local injectivity of the presheaf quotient map, so the same cited local-bijection criterion gives the isomorphism of sheafifications. The generic quotient theorem applies over arbitrary $S$ and does not assume a rational section. Since smooth scheme charts are locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $P\to S$ is locally of finite presentation in the convention of the statement.

proof.text: Tensor product, the trivial bundle and duality give multiplication, identity and inversion on the presheaf $T\mapsto\operatorname{Pic}(C_T)$; pullback respects each. Using the local representative and local equality properties established in step 3, on sheaf sections, choose a common fppf refinement with bundle representatives and apply these operations there. Replacing representatives only changes their classes by locally trivial differences, so the resulting sections agree on overlaps and glue uniquely. Associativity, commutativity, the identity and inverse equations hold on this cover by the corresponding bundle isomorphisms, hence hold in the sheaf. By [def-trf-algebraic-space], morphisms of spaces are natural transformations of their sheaves. Therefore these operations themselves give maps $P\times_SP\to P$, $S\to P$ and $P\to P$, with the asserted equations, making $P$ a commutative group algebraic space and identifying its law with tensor product.

source.place: section-pic-functor, group structure from tensor product

proof.text: Test the diagonal on a scheme $T\to P\times_SP$, given by sections $s,t\in P(T)$. By the local representative property established in step 3, choose an fppf covering $T_i\to T$ on which they are represented by line bundles $V_i,W_i$ on $C_{T_i}$. Put $L_i=V_i\otimes W_i^{-1}$. The morphism $C_{T_i}\to T_i$ retains properness, flatness and finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], and the universal structure-sheaf hypothesis persists because every $T_i$-scheme is an $S$-scheme. Apply [lem-sc-picard-diagonal-locally-closed] to this morphism and the rank-one bundle $L_i$. It gives an immersion $Z_i\to T_i$ of finite presentation. For any $T'\to T_i$, its factorization criterion is equivalent to $L_i|_{C_{T'}}=f_{T'}^*N$ for an invertible $N$ on $T'$. Indeed the cited node initially gives a finite locally free $N$; every fibre of $C_{T'}\to T'$ is nonempty, since over a residue field the universal structure-sheaf hypothesis gives $H^0(C_{t'},\mathcal O)=\kappa(t')\ne0$. Pulling back to a point of that fibre forces the rank of $N$ at $t'$ to be one. Finally [lem-pc-pic-exact] says exactly that a line bundle has zero Picard sheaf class if and only if it is pulled back from the base. Hence $Z_i$ represents the equality functor $s|_{T_i}=t|_{T_i}$, including all nonreduced test schemes, not only its point set.

source.place: Tag 0D2D, lemma-diagonal-pic, reduction to the pullback locus; more-morphisms.tex Tag 0BDP

proof.text: The base change $E=T\times_{P\times_SP}P$ of the diagonal is already an algebraic space. Its pullback to $T_i$ is the equality functor just represented by $Z_i$, so is a quasi-compact immersion: finite presentation includes quasi-compactness. Apply [lem-sfb-space-quasi-compact-immersion-locality] to $E\to T$ and the fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$. Thus $E\to T$ is a quasi-compact immersion, including representability by a scheme. As this holds for every scheme test $T\to P\times_SP$, the diagonal is representable by quasi-compact immersions. Its quasi-compactness is precisely the quasi-separatedness of $P\to S$ in the statement, and the immersion clause also follows.
